title: Production-Driven Patch Generation and Validation
authors: Thomas Durieux; Youssef Hamadi; Martin Monperrus
venue_or_publisher: arXiv:1609.06848; short version ICSE 2017 NIER track ('Production-Driven Patch Generation') [verify track year]
central_claim: Itzal: production oracles (uncaught exceptions; optionally domain-specific oracles such as schema compliance) detect a failing request, a sandboxed patch search replays it, candidate patches are regression-checked on shadow production traffic, and surviving patches are reported to developers (dashboard; automated GitHub PRs envisioned). Evaluated on 34 production failures (14 apps) and 16 seeded failures in 3 e-commerce apps.
cite_claim: The idea of turning a production failure into a source patch validated on production traffic and handed to developers (possibly as a PR) dates to at least 2016 (Itzal); its oracles were exceptions/HTTP codes and its patches were template-based (NPE), with no committed reproduction test.
location: Abstract; Sec. 1; Sec. 3.1.1 (Request-oracle); Sec. 3.2.5 (Communication with the developer); Sec. 4.2 Answer to RQ2
quote: it uses production oracles (such as uncaught exceptions) to detect failures and trigger patch search.
relevance: Closest research prior art to the full fiks loop (observe -> repair -> validate -> hand to developer). fiks must cite it and position against it: fiks's oracle is a semantic contract on successful tool output, its validation artifact is a committed F->P test from recorded upstream HTTP plus CI, and its patcher is an LLM coding agent.

title: Automatically Patching Errors in Deployed Software (ClearView)
authors: Jeff H. Perkins; Sunghun Kim; Sam Larsen; Saman Amarasinghe; et al.; Michael D. Ernst; Martin Rinard
central_claim: Learns invariants from normal executions, detects failures with runtime monitors, generates binary patches that enforce violated invariants, and keeps the patches that work in the deployed community.
cite_claim: Invariant learning -> runtime violation -> automatic patch -> in-production evaluation was demonstrated in 2009 (ClearView), as runtime binary patching rather than source-level PRs.
location: Abstract; Sec. 1 (verified by sibling area llm-repair)
quote: observes normal executions to learn invariants that characterize the application's normal behavior
relevance: Foundational self-healing loop; weakens any claim that 'invariant-violation-driven repair' is new. Difference: runtime state/binary patch, no human review, no source test.

title: Exterminator: Automatically Correcting Memory Errors with High Probability
authors: Gene Novark; Emery D. Berger; Benjamin G. Zorn
venue_or_publisher: PLDI 2007 [verify venue from proceedings page; PDF filename pldi028]
central_claim: Detects heap memory errors via randomization, derives runtime patches that fix them in current and subsequent executions, and merges patches generated by multiple users (collaborative correction).
cite_claim: 'Fix once, every user benefits' was already realised in 2007 for memory errors via collaborative merging of runtime patches (Exterminator).
quote: Exterminator enables collaborative bug correction by merging patches generated by multiple users.
relevance: Prior art for fiks's 'fixed for every agent' framing; differs in fault class (memory safety), patch form (runtime allocator patches) and absence of source tests/PRs.

title: Finding and fixing software bugs automatically with SapFix and Sapienz
central_claim: Sapienz finds crashes and designs tests; SapFix generates patches, validates them with developer and Sapienz tests and sends them to human reviewers; it does not deploy fixes on its own.
cite_claim: Industrial detect -> test -> patch -> human review loops exist for crashes (SapFix/Sapienz).
location: Blog body (verified by sibling area llm-repair)
quote: is not designed to deploy fixes to production code on its own
relevance: Covers Reproduce+Repair+Ship for crash oracles found by pre-release search-based testing; no runtime semantic oracle on successful output.

title: Agentic Program Repair from Test Failures at Scale: A Neuro-symbolic approach with static analysis and test execution feedback
authors: Chandra Maddila; Adam Tait; et al.; Peter C. Rigby
central_claim: A ReAct-style agent triggered by triaged test failures proposes fixes with static-analysis and test-execution feedback and an LLM judge; in production 80% of fixes were reviewed and 31.5% of reviewed fixes landed.
cite_claim: Agentic repair from failing tests is deployed at industrial scale with human review; it starts from an existing failing test rather than from a runtime observation.
location: Abstract; Sec. IX (verified by sibling llm-repair; abstract re-fetched 2026-10-21)
quote: Of those that received a review, 31.5% were accepted.
relevance: Covers Repair+Gate+Ship given a failing test; shows the repair half of fiks is industrial practice. Merge-rate anchor next to C21/C22.

title: LangSmith Engine (documentation)
central_claim: Engine scans tracing projects on a schedule and on feedback signals, clusters recurring issues, diagnoses root cause against traces and connected source, creates dataset examples, can replay an issue's traces (beta) and opens draft PRs it never merges; supports Deep Agents/LangChain/LangGraph apps.
cite_claim: LangSmith Engine closes a trace -> issue -> diagnosis -> draft-PR loop for LangChain-family agents, validates by replaying traces and offline datasets, and never merges; the docs do not say it writes test code.
location: Engine page: triggers; validation; pull requests; supported frameworks
quote: Diagnoses the root cause against your traces and connected source code
relevance: Closest commercial loop. Differs: fixes the agent app not the tool server; scheduled LLM-driven discovery rather than inline contract check; no deterministic F-gated test; no receipt to the running agent.

title: Signal (Arize AX documentation)
central_claim: Signal scans traces every 6 h by default, groups recurring failures into issues with a proposed prompt/code/config/eval fix, and on Enterprise can open pull requests for proposed fixes.
cite_claim: Arize Signal turns scheduled trace scans into issues and (Enterprise) fix PRs; tests are not described.
location: Signal docs: schedule; issues; proposed fix; plan limits
quote: can open pull requests for proposed fixes
relevance: Second trace->PR competitor; covers Observe(batch, LLM)+Repair+Ship; no repro gate.

title: Anatomy of a pull request (PostHog Self-driving)
central_claim: Signals (error tracking, replay, tickets) become reports; actionable reports lead an implementation agent to open a PR containing a regression test reproducing the failure; the agent babysits CI until green after opening; humans merge.
cite_claim: PostHog Self-driving PRs include a regression test that reproduces the original failure, and CI is fixed after the PR opens; the page does not require the test to fail on the original code.
quote: a regression test that reproduces the original failure
relevance: Strongest product prior art for 'repro test inside the PR'. Differs from fiks: no stated F gate, CI after PR, error/UX triggers.

title: Self-driving (PostHog docs)
central_claim: Self-driving turns signals from error tracking, session replay, logs and external tools into reports and opens PRs for actionable ones; humans review and merge.
cite_claim: PostHog's open-beta Self-driving converts product signals into reviewed PRs.
location: Self-driving overview (verified by sibling area observability)
quote: When a report is actionable, PostHog opens a pull request for you to review and merge.
relevance: Context for posthog-anatomy-pr.

title: Issue Fix (Seer)
central_claim: Seer uses issue details, tracing data, logs and profiles plus linked repos to root-cause and fix issues, optionally drafting a PR or handing off to a coding agent; automatic runs require >=10 events in 14 days and a fixability score; regression tests only on request; CI iteration after the PR.
cite_claim: Error-tracking autofix starts from Sentry issues and needs recurrence (>=10 events/14 days) for automatic runs; reproduction tests are optional and user-requested (reuse C27).
location: Issue Fix page: Inputs; Automation; PR iteration
quote: Automated attempts are limited to prevent an endless loop.
relevance: Reuse C27. Covers Repair+Ship(+CI after PR) from error signals. A silent wrong value never becomes a Sentry issue unless something throws.

title: Bits AI Dev Agent / Bits Code
central_claim: Generates fixes from Error Tracking, APM recommendations, code security and other Datadog signals, on demand or autonomously; monitors CI logs to fix failures and merge blockers; never auto-merges.
cite_claim: Datadog Bits Code opens fix PRs from observability signals and iterates on CI, never auto-merging.
location: Bits Code docs: supported products; CI auto-fix; merge policy
quote: Bits Code never auto-merges PRs or MRs.
relevance: Error/APM-triggered; same 'never merge' policy as fiks, so that is not a differentiator.

title: AI SRE (Investigations)
central_claim: When an incident is declared, Investigations correlates telemetry, code changes and past incidents to name the root cause; its only change action is a PR the user reviews and merges.
cite_claim: AI SRE products go from declared incidents to root cause and reviewed PRs.
quote: a pull request you review and merge yourself
relevance: Incident-triggered (loud failures); shows the PR-as-output pattern is industry standard by 2026.

title: Composio MCP Gateway (product page)
central_claim: Claims gateway-side 'tools that fix themselves' (schema drift, malformed params, rate limits) learned from production calls and published to every agent; worked example triggered by a recurring 400 error; no tests, review or staged rollout described; payloads never stored.
cite_claim: Composio markets self-patching of its managed toolkits from production call patterns, published to all agents; its public example is error-triggered and validation is not described.
location: 'Tools that fix themselves' section; Enterprise deployment section (re-fetched 2026-10-21)
quote: Tools learn from real production calls and patch without your agent noticing.
relevance: Strongest commercial counter-example to 'fix once for every agent'. Vendor-internal, error-triggered, unaudited; cannot be run as a baseline.

title: ADAPTIX: self-healing tool registry for AI agents under runtime API schema drift
authors: P. Patil; N. Shidne; S. Tawde; O. Ekbote
central_claim: Repairs a tool definition (new tool version) when a failed 400/422 call coincides with a live-schema change; probes and verifies response shape only; autonomous, no human approval; no tests or PRs.
cite_claim: Self-healing MCP-style registries repair tool definitions after error+schema-diff triggers and explicitly do not check business meaning of results.
quote: proves the shape of the result, not its business meaning
relevance: Closest OSS 'self-healing tool' prototype; its own README concedes fiks's target class (silent semantic drift) is out of scope.

title: MCP-Healer: Self-Healing Runtime Middleware & Schema Mutation Adapter for MCP Tools
central_claim: Proxy middleware that rewrites agent-sent payloads after schema validation errors or HTTP 400s.
cite_claim: 'Self-healing' MCP middleware repairs input payloads after explicit errors, not wrong outputs.
location: README header (verified by sibling area mcp-market)
quote: Intercepts schema validation errors, 400 Bad Requests, and signature drifts
relevance: Shows the term 'self-healing MCP' is already used, for a different (input, error-driven) problem.

title: self-healing-api-agent
central_claim: Diffs two versions of a third-party OpenAPI spec, finds affected code and opens a ready-to-review PR; does not watch live endpoints; running the target repo's tests is an unchecked roadmap item.
cite_claim: Spec-diff-driven 'self-healing' agents open PRs but cannot see behavioural drift with an unchanged spec and do not run tests (reuse C27).
quote: diffs published spec files, not live endpoints
relevance: Reuse C27. Runnable baseline: on fiks's byte-identical spec it should produce no change.

title: ApiPatch (PyPI package apipatch)
central_claim: LLM agent that audits a repo for deprecated third-party API calls using model knowledge plus fetched docs/changelogs and opens PRs; validation is AST/syntax checks, not the project's tests.
cite_claim: ApiPatch fixes breaking changes the LLM or published changelogs already know about and opens PRs without running the project's tests (reuse C27).
location: PyPI JSON metadata (info.summary, description), fetched 2026-10-21; the 0.8.2 HTML page cited in C27 did not render for us
quote: Autonomous AI Agent that detects and fixes deprecated API calls in Python, JS, TS via LLM-powered Pull Requests.
relevance: Reuse C27 (update version/URL). MIT, runnable baseline for 'knowledge-driven' repair.

title: Tusk Drift (API tests from live traffic)
central_claim: SDK records inbound/outbound traffic (HTTP, GraphQL, gRPC, DB, Redis); replays inbound calls while serving outbound calls from recordings; on PRs classifies deviations as intended or unintended, performs root-cause analysis and suggests code fixes.
cite_claim: Traffic-to-test products already add AI root-cause analysis and fix suggestions, but they trigger on the team's own code changes and replay recorded dependency responses.
location: API tests overview: record; replay; detect; cloud
quote: replays the inbound API call while intercepting outbound requests and serving them from recorded data
relevance: Covers Capture+Reproduce(record/replay)+fix suggestion; closest traffic-to-test competitor. Because outbound calls are served from recordings, an upstream behavioural drift is invisible to it unless re-recorded (inference to test).

title: What is Keploy?
central_claim: Records live API traffic at the socket level (eBPF), stores unique interactions as test cases with dependency mocks, replays and compares new responses to recorded ones.
cite_claim: Keploy turns production traffic into regression tests whose oracle is the previously recorded response, with dependencies mocked from recordings.
quote: all the unique network interactions are stored within Keploy server as a test-case.
relevance: OSS (Apache-2.0) runnable traffic-to-test baseline.

title: Speedscale documentation
central_claim: Captures real API traffic, turns inbound requests into replayable tests and dependency traffic into mocks, and replays against code changes before release; no code fixing described.
cite_claim: Traffic replay platforms validate a service's code changes against recorded traffic; they do not repair code.
quote: Speedscale captures real API traffic from your running services and replays it against code changes before release.
relevance: Capture+Reproduce only; commercial.

title: GoReplay
central_claim: Passively captures live HTTP traffic and replays it into test environments for shadowing and load testing; no assertion or repair capability described.
cite_claim: Shadow-traffic tools provide capture and replay, not oracles or fixes.
quote: an open-source tool for capturing and replaying live HTTP traffic into a test environment
relevance: Capture only; license split between OSS core and PRO [verify exact core license].

title: Diffy
central_claim: Proxy that multicasts each request to candidate, primary and secondary instances and flags regressions when candidate-primary disagreement exceeds primary-secondary noise.
cite_claim: Differential testing on live traffic detects behavioural regressions without hand-written assertions, using old behaviour as the oracle.
quote: Diffy finds regressions in your service by running your new code and your old code side by side
relevance: A detection baseline we could run unmodified (NC-ND licence: non-commercial, no adaptation): v1 vendor as primary/secondary, v2 as candidate. Detects drift but has no notion of which side is right, and no repair.

title: Meticulous
central_claim: Records user sessions to generate visual end-to-end tests with replayed backend responses and maintains the suite automatically; does not modify application code.
cite_claim: Session-recording test generators maintain tests, not code.
quote: generates a continuously evolving test suite
relevance: Frontend analogue of traffic-to-test; out of scope for repair.

title: OpenAPI contract drift detection
central_claim: Compares live proxied/mocked traffic against the uploaded OpenAPI spec, groups drift events (schema, params, headers, status; lists 'behavioral drift') and proposes AI spec patches applied only after human approval.
cite_claim: Traffic-vs-spec drift tools patch the spec, not the code, and detect structural mismatches; behavioural-drift detection is named but not described.
location: Drift detection page: drift types; AI patches; approval
quote: nothing is automatic
relevance: Observe(structural)+Ship(spec patch). Opposite repair direction to fiks: it makes the spec match reality rather than the client code match the contract.

title: Systems and Methods for Detecting Silent Backward-Incompatible API Contract Drift Using Runtime Structural-Semantic Fingerprints
venue_or_publisher: Technical Disclosure Commons, Defensive Publications Series 10178
central_claim: Defensive publication: learn endpoint-specific behavioural invariants (presence, type stability, nullability, cross-field rules) from historical traffic, fingerprint runtime responses and alert on silent backward-incompatible drift; no tests, fixes or PRs.
cite_claim: A 2026 defensive publication from Visa covers learning invariants from API traffic to detect silent contract drift, limited to detection and alerting.
quote: learning endpoint-specific behavioral invariants from historical API traffic
relevance: Patent-adjacent prior art for fiks's Observe step and for contract inference from v1 traffic; puts that step in the public domain.

title: Postman Insights overview
central_claim: Traffic-based API observability with per-endpoint metrics and errors, endpoint inference, and a Repro Mode to recreate failing calls from real request/response context; no test generation or code fixes described.
cite_claim: Traffic-based API observability can recreate failing calls from production context but stops at error-level detection.
quote: automatic per-endpoint metrics and errors across all your API endpoints
relevance: Capture+manual repro for errors; Akita lineage per sibling api-contracts (postman-akita-2023).

title: Outcome Monitors: Recovery Affordances for Silent Tool Failures
central_claim: Deterministic per-call contract checks mined from clean traces attach nonbinding receipts naming recovery tools; ToolMaze completion 10.9% -> 28.1%; out-of-vocabulary detection ~46%; the monitor never repairs and organic recovery is left open.
cite_claim: The closest research system to fiks's Observe+receipt step explicitly does not execute any repair and leaves recovery from organic failures open (reuse C11).
quote: never restricts an action, executes a repair, reveals a benchmark fault label, or consults the evaluator
relevance: Reuse C11. fiks's Observe step is close to this; the paper's stated non-goal (repair) is fiks's contribution.

title: Agent Lifecycle Toolkit (ALTK): Silent Review
central_claim: Prompt-based LLM reviewer that labels each tool response as accomplished/partial/not accomplished to catch silent errors; no repair.
cite_claim: A shipped open-source component already detects silent tool errors with an LLM judge, without repair.
location: Silent Review doc: overview (verified by sibling area mcp-market)
quote: A prompt-based component to automatically identify silent errors in tool calls - errors that do not produce explicit error messages.
relevance: Detection-only baseline (Apache-2.0) runnable on fiks drifts.

title: Byam: Fixing Breaking Dependency Updates with Large Language Models
authors: Frank Reyes; May Mahmoud; Federico Bono; Sarah Nadi; Benoit Baudry; Martin Monperrus
central_claim: LLM repair of client code broken by dependency API changes (compilation/build failures) on BUMP; best model (o3-mini) fully fixes 27% of builds and 78% of individual compilation errors.
cite_claim: LLM repair of client code after upstream (library) API changes is studied, but the trigger is a compile/build failure, not a silent behavioural change.
quote: can break existing client code
relevance: Nearest research analogue for 'upstream changed, fix the client'; loud trigger only.

title: BUMP: A Benchmark of Reproducible Breaking Dependency Updates
authors: Frank Reyes; Yogya Gamage; Gabriel Skoglund; Benoit Baudry; Martin Monperrus
central_claim: 571 reproducible breaking dependency updates from 153 Maven projects, with categorised build-failure causes.
cite_claim: Existing benchmarks of upstream-induced breakage (BUMP) are build-failure benchmarks for library dependencies, not silent web-API drift.
quote: the first of its kind
relevance: Shows a benchmark gap fiks's drift suite can fill; potential design template (reproducible pairs).

title: About Dependabot version updates
central_claim: Opens PRs that bump outdated dependency versions; does not detect behavioural changes or edit application code; users verify compatibility with their own tests and changelogs.
cite_claim: Dependabot, the model the YC RFS invokes (C13), only bumps versions and leaves behavioural compatibility to the user's tests.
quote: check that your tests pass, review the changelog and release notes included in the pull request summary
relevance: Frames C13's 'Dependabot for APIs' ask: fiks supplies the missing behavioural oracle.

title: feat(core): Add an internal self-healing agent (no-changelog)
central_claim: Adds an internal, default-off self-healing agent that investigates a failed workflow execution against a captured baseline with an injected verifier; no automatic trigger; closed without merging on 2026-10-15.
cite_claim: Workflow platforms are prototyping self-healing agents for failed executions (failure-triggered, verifier-gated), not yet shipped (reuse C27; PR closed unmerged).
quote: adds no automatic trigger or public launch endpoint
relevance: Reuse C27 with correction: the PR was closed without merge on 2026-10-15.

title: Optic
central_claim: OpenAPI linting, diffing and breaking-change checks plus spec generation and verification from test traffic; archived after Optic Labs joined Atlassian.
cite_claim: Traffic-assisted spec tools exist but operate at the spec level, and the leading OSS one is archived.
quote: This repository was archived by the owner on Jan 12, 2026.
relevance: Spec-level baseline class (with oasdiff, C27).

title: AI Assist (Connector Builder)
central_claim: AI Assist pre-fills and suggests connector configuration at build time; the docs describe no monitoring of running connectors or automatic repair after API changes.
cite_claim: AI-maintained connector tooling (Airbyte) is build-time assistance, not runtime detection or repair.
quote: you should still review the output to ensure everything is set up correctly.
relevance: Negative result for the 'AI-maintained connectors' hypothesis in our search.

title: Human-competitive Patches in Automatic Program Repair with Repairnator
authors: Martin Monperrus; Simon Urli; Thomas Durieux; Matias Martinez; Benoit Baudry; Lionel Seinturier
central_claim: A bot monitors CI build failures in OSS, reproduces them, synthesises patches and proposes them as PRs, some merged by maintainers.
cite_claim: Bots that turn CI failures into repair PRs have existed since 2018 (Repairnator).
quote: Repairnator is a bot. It constantly monitors software bugs discovered during continuous integration of open-source software
relevance: Covers Reproduce(CI failure)+Repair+Ship; trigger is a failing build.

title: Copilot Autofix for code scanning
central_claim: Turns code-scanning alerts into suggested fixes or draft PRs and validates them by re-running CodeQL.
cite_claim: Detector-as-oracle repair (the alerting detector re-validates the fix) is established for static alerts.
location: Autofix concepts (verified by sibling area observability)
quote: Copilot validates fixes by re-running CodeQL with the code scanning query suite.
relevance: Analogue of fiks's 'the violated contract is the oracle', but static rather than runtime.

title: mcp-eval
central_claim: Evaluation framework that runs real agents against real MCP servers with assertions and OTel traces from test runs; generates tests from tool definitions; no live-traffic monitoring or repair.
cite_claim: MCP testing frameworks generate tests from tool definitions, not from runtime violations.
quote: No mocks, actual agent-to-server communication
relevance: Pre-deployment MCP testing; complementary, not competing. Licence inconsistent in README [verify].
